sections.h2: Which Santa Rosa County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Santa Rosa County divides the job three ways. The Property Appraiser (SRCPA, at srcpa.gov) sets values and exemptions, the Tax Collector (srctc.com) mails and collects the bill, and a Value Adjustment Board hears appeals.

The Tax Collector's pages explain the chain: the appraiser sets assessed value and decides exemption eligibility, the county commission, school board and other levying bodies set millage, and the appraiser then builds the roll and certifies it to the collector, who prints and mails the notices. Bills go to the owner's last address on the roll, and a mortgage company that pays through escrow should request the bill. The collector runs offices in Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay.

The appraiser's home page reports county statistics that show the scale of the roll: about 99.4 thousand residential properties, 8 thousand commercial, 5.4 thousand agricultural, and a taxable county value of 20.29 billion dollars.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address: Property Appraiser.
  • Bill, payment, delinquency, certificates: Tax Collector.
  • Appeals of assessments, denied exemptions and deferrals: Value Adjustment Board, made up of three county commissioners and two school board members or a special master.

sections.h2: What is the Santa Rosa County payment schedule?
sections.html:
Tax statements are normally mailed on or before November 1 for the January through December tax year, and the gross amount is due by March 31. Early payment earns a discount that drops each month.

Santa Rosa County Tax Collector discount schedule for real estate
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3% penalty; advertising fees added May 1

The collector adds that if a discount period ends on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the discount runs to the next business day. It is the taxpayer's job to make sure a bill is received, so call the office if nothing has arrived by mid-November.

sections.h2: What happens if Santa Rosa County taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1, and after that only cashier's check, money order, cash or credit card are accepted. The date the office receives the payment determines the amount due.

Florida law has the collector advertise delinquent parcels in a local newspaper once a week for three weeks, and the county commission awards that job to the paper with the lowest bid. The cost lands on the delinquent bill. On or before June 1 the collector holds the tax certificate sale online through LienHub.com, as a reverse auction that opens at 18 percent interest and goes to the lowest bidder.

  • A certificate is a lien, and the office states that buying one gives no ownership rights.
  • Unpaid amounts rise right away if the county holds the certificate and it is purchased, or if a tax deed application is made.
  • The office warns that losing the property is possible when taxes stay unpaid.

Under the state statute summary, a certificate holder may file for a tax deed only after two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, and the holder may not contact the owner to demand payment during those two years. Homestead parcels also carry an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.

A seller facing this should get a current payoff figure from the Tax Collector, since the number changes as costs are added.

sections.h2: How do Santa Rosa County homestead filing dates work?
sections.html:
The appraiser's Dates to Remember box lists a homestead filing period from January 1, 2027 to March 1, 2027. The same box gives January 1 to June 1, 2027 for the Persons 65 or Over exemption and for the Deployed Service Member exemption.

Filing is online. Search for your parcel on the appraiser's site, then click Apply for Exemptions, after updating your Florida ID and vehicle registration to the home address. Florida's state revenue agency sets the base rules: the owner must make the property the permanent residence by January 1 and file with the county property appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 of the exemption applies to all levies, and the additional amount applies only to non-school levies on value above $50,000.

State law also lets a county or city grant an extra exemption of up to $50,000 to seniors 65 and older within an income limit, by ordinance, and a 25-year version for homes under $250,000 in just value. Ask the appraiser which of those Santa Rosa taxing authorities have adopted. Veterans with a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more may qualify for a $5,000 reduction under ss. 196.081 and 196.091.

sections.h2: What changes at a Santa Rosa County sale?
sections.html:
Selling resets the property to just value for the next owner, and the seller's exemptions leave with the seller. Florida defines change of ownership broadly: a sale, foreclosure or transfer of legal or beneficial title, except where the same person stays entitled or a spouse transfers.

Santa Rosa's appraiser sends a Property Owner Protection Alert about letters that offer a copy of your deed for a fee. The businesses mailing them have no official capacity, and the offices of the Property Appraiser and the Clerk of Courts did not approve or take part in those mailings. A seller who gets one after closing can ignore the fee offer and ask the Clerk for the deed.

Documentary stamps on a deed run $0.70 per $100 of price, and consideration includes any mortgage the buyer assumes. Tax is paid to the Clerk at recording. If a tax certificate or tax deed matter exists, the deed sale rules in s. 197.542 require the winning bidder to post a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is more.

sections.h2: How can a Santa Rosa County seller handle tax due at closing?
sections.html:
Ask the closing agent to order a tax payoff and apply it at closing. The collector's online parcel search shows the balance, and the branches in Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay can answer questions in person. Keep the escrow position in mind too: if a lender pays your taxes, the mortgage company requests the bill, and the payoff still needs confirming before closing.

The collector's pages are explicit about who answers what. Questions on legal description, value, exemptions and name or address changes belong with the appraiser at srcpa.gov, while rates belong to the taxing authorities that hold advertised public hearings. Non-ad valorem charges, which the collector says typically cover fire departments, street lighting, paving and special local projects, come from local levying agencies, so ask the agency named on the bill.

For a deeper bill review, ask the appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since the gap is the Save Our Homes benefit the buyer will lose. The state revenue agency lists a 3.4% CPI for 2024 with a 3.0% cap, 2.9% for 2025 and 2.7% for 2026.

faqs.q: What is the Santa Rosa County payment schedule?
faqs.a: The gross amount is due by March 31, with bills mailed on or before November 1. Payments in November earn 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Santa Rosa County taxes?
faqs.a: A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1 for unpaid real estate accounts. Advertising fees are added on May 1, and a tax certificate sale follows by June 1.

faqs.q: Where do I file Santa Rosa County homestead?
faqs.a: File online through the Property Appraiser's parcel page using the Apply for Exemptions button. The posted homestead period runs January 1 to March 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Who hears a Santa Rosa County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Value Adjustment Board. It hears denied exemptions, assessment petitions and tax deferral appeals. the state revenue agency sets a 25 day window after the TRIM notice for a value petition.

faqs.q: Does the county sell my house when I miss a payment?
faqs.a: Not directly. The county sells a tax certificate, which is a lien starting at 18 percent interest, and only a later tax deed application can lead to a sale of the property.
